name: Securo
description: Securo is a self-hosted personal finance manager: accounts, transactions, budgets, goals, assets and reports, with imports from OFX, QIF, CAMT and CSV and optional bank sync for European, US and Brazilian banks. Upstream runs it as six containers; this image puts the official backend and web app, the Celery worker and the scheduler into one. Getting started: • PostgreSQL already running? Enter its host, user and password. It needs pgvector, which pgvector/pgvector:pg16 and the PostgreSQL image Immich uses both have and the plain postgres image does not. Securo creates its database on the first start if the user may. • Redis already running? Enter its host. If other apps use database 0 on it, give Securo another number under Redis database. • No PostgreSQL or Redis? Set Built-in PostgreSQL and Built-in Redis to true and leave their host fields empty. • Set App address to the address you open Securo on. Bank sync and single sign-on send you back there. • The first start creates the tables, which takes under a minute. Securo is ready when the log says SECURO IS READY. Then open the web app and create your account. Passkeys only work over HTTPS on a domain, not on http://IP:port. Behind a reverse proxy, set Trusted proxies to 2. Source on GitHub: https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/securo This is an independent packaging of Securo and is not affiliated with the Securo project.

paths.name: Data
paths.description: Attachments, secrets.env with the generated secret key, the secrets folder for an Enable Banking key and, with Built-in PostgreSQL and Redis, their data.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: Port of the Securo web app.

variables.name: App address
variables.description: The address you open Securo on, such as http://192.168.1.10:3000 or https://securo.example.com. Bank sync and single sign-on send you back there.

variables.name: Built-in PostgreSQL
variables.description: true runs PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector inside this container, with its data in the Data folder. Leave it false to use your own PostgreSQL.

variables.name: Database host
variables.description: IP or name of your PostgreSQL server. It needs pgvector. Leave it empty with Built-in PostgreSQL.

variables.name: Database user
variables.description: A user that may create databases, or the owner of a database you created for Securo. Not used with Built-in PostgreSQL.

variables.name: Database password
variables.description: Password of the database user. It must not contain @ or %. Not used with Built-in PostgreSQL.

variables.name: Built-in Redis
variables.description: true runs Redis inside this container. Leave it false to use your own Redis.

variables.name: Redis host
variables.description: IP or name of your Redis server. Leave it empty with Built-in Redis.

variables.name: Registration
variables.description: Whether new people can sign up. Set it to false once your own account exists.

variables.name: Database port
variables.description: Port of your PostgreSQL server.

variables.name: Database name
variables.description: Created on the first start if it does not exist and the user may create databases.

variables.name: Redis port
variables.description: Port of your Redis server.

variables.name: Redis password
variables.description: Only when your Redis server asks for one.

variables.name: Redis database
variables.description: Database number on your Redis server. Give Securo one no other app uses, since its task queue shares the name every Celery app uses.

variables.name: Trusted proxies
variables.description: How many proxies stand in front of Securo, counting the one inside this container. 1 without a reverse proxy, 2 behind one. The login rate limit counts visitors by the address this finds.

variables.name: Secret key
variables.description: Signs the login tokens. Leave it empty to get a generated one, kept in secrets.env. Changing it signs everyone out.

variables.name: Enable Banking app ID
variables.description: Bank sync for about 2500 European banks. Put the application's private key into the secrets folder of the Data folder as enable_banking_private.pem. The redirect URL to register is your App address followed by /oauth/callback, over https.

variables.name: SimpleFIN
variables.description: Bank sync for US and other banks through the SimpleFIN Bridge. You paste a setup token into Securo under Accounts.

variables.name: SimpleFIN bridge
variables.description: The beta bridge hands out demo tokens for trying it. For real banks use https://bridge.simplefin.org.

variables.name: Pluggy client ID
variables.description: Bank sync for Brazilian banks, from dashboard.pluggy.ai.

variables.name: Pluggy client secret
variables.description: The client secret that belongs to the Pluggy client ID.

variables.name: OIDC
variables.description: Sign-in through Authentik, Pocket ID or another OIDC provider. The redirect URI to register is your App address followed by /api/auth/oidc/callback.

variables.name: OIDC provider name
variables.description: Shown on the sign-in button.

variables.name: OIDC discovery URL
variables.description: Ends in /.well-known/openid-configuration.

variables.name: OIDC client ID
variables.description: From the application you created at your provider.

variables.name: OIDC client secret
variables.description: From the application you created at your provider.

variables.name: Password sign-in
variables.description: false allows only OIDC sign-in. Securo refuses to start that way until OIDC is fully set up.

variables.name: Open Exchange Rates app ID
variables.description: Optional key for exchange rates between your currencies, from openexchangerates.org.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: User that owns the files in the Data folder. 99 is nobody on Unraid.

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group that owns the files in the Data folder. 100 is users on Unraid.
